title: Diversity types: neutral, phylogenetic and functional

title: Profiles, evenness and redundancy
text: Neutral diversity counts taxa; phylogenetic functional diversity count distinct lineages trait combinations. taxa closely related functionally similar, much neutral diversity redundant — losing taxon costs little unique phylogenetic/functional diversity. hillred() quantifies fitting saturating relationship neutral diversity (x) phylogenetic/functional diversity (y) across samples, y = -· 2^(-x / b) + c, summarising redundancy 1 - b / max(x). therefore needs tree dist, several samples fit curve: returned table redundancy summary plus fitted , b, c coefficients per order. Values near 1 mean assemblage highly redundant (taxa phylogenetically/functionally interchangeable); values near 0 mean taxon contributes largely unique diversity. Like profile, result ready-made plot() method. draws fit behind redundancy number: sample’s neutral diversity phylogenetic/functional diversity, fitted saturating curve per order. curve bends early plateaus signals high redundancy.
